## Goal

A person can sign out: of the server's sign-in, of an operator's own page that signs them in through it, and of a hosted page they signed in on, so a shared computer never hands the next person the previous one's account; and an idle server with an operator module writes no more often than its operator chooses.

## Owned requirements

None: a maintenance or design unit owns no requirement (D152). Its progress report's evidence table has one row per item of its scope, each closed by a check through the real public interface (README §3), and the checks it adds extend their owners' rows.

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- a sign-out on the API origin: `POST /signout` ends the browser's sign-in session there (its `browser_session` row and its cookie), from every page of the API origin that shows who is signed in ("Signed in as Ada · Sign out" on the sign-in, device, consent and "Answer as yourself" pages), so the next sign-in in that browser asks the person's provider again;
- the same sign-out for an operator's own page (an `operatorClients` client): the page sends the person to the server's sign-out, which ends the session and returns them to an address the client registered, so the operator's one "Sign out" signs the person out of both;
- `prompt=login` on `/oauth/authorize`, so a client can ask for a fresh sign-in with the provider whatever the browser's session (OpenID Connect Core §3.1.2.1);
- a "Sign out" in a hosted page's viewer chip, behind the shell's session, its CSRF token and its own `Origin`: the page's session goes back to the route's anonymous viewer, and a later "Sign in" there asks again;
- expired sign-in sessions and sign-ins in progress removed by a sweep, so the directory keeps only live ones;
- an operator's metering window as a server setting (`metering.windowSeconds`, #203), windows aligned to the clock, so an idle server with an operator module writes less often.

Design detail for this package:

- A maintenance unit (D152): it owns no requirement. Its scope is the GitHub milestone `MT-06` (#204, #203), each item closed with its check through the real interface (a real `mostra-runtime server` with its fake providers and a metadata-document client, as WP-30's and MT-05's sign-in suites run them, and the real shell in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit for the hosted page) and a seeded violation red on the old code; the checks it adds extend HY-08's (sign-in and sessions) and MC-04's (the authorization server) rows.
- **The finding** (#204). The API origin's sign-in is a 7-day browser session (`browser_session`, the `__Host-mostra-signin` cookie; INTERFACES §18.5, D167 item 10). Nothing ends it: the server has no sign-out and never removes a row. An operator's own page (an `operatorClients` client) ends its own session, but its next "Sign in" goes to the authorization server, which still has the person's session and consent and returns them at once without their provider. A hosted page's "Sign in" binds the route's shell session to the account with no way back. On a shared computer the next person at that browser can, for up to 7 days, act as the previous one on the operator's page, the device page (approving a code links *their* machine to the previous person's account), a chat app's consent, and every hosted page the previous person signed in to.
- **Sign-out on the API origin.** `POST /signout`, a form of the API origin's own pages with its own `Origin` and a CSRF token derived from the session (as consent's, D167 item 10), ends the session: its row is removed and its cookie cleared, and the person lands on a page that says they are signed out, with the operator's footer (D171). Every page of the API origin that shows who is signed in carries "Signed in as Ada · Sign out": the sign-in page reached with a session, the device page, the consent page and "Answer as yourself". A GET never ends anything (D98's side-effect-free GETs): a sign-out link for another origin is a page with one button.
- **Sign-out for an operator's own page.** An `operatorClients` client signs a person out of the server's sign-in from its own "Sign out". Design it twice and choose (D123): (a) the client's page posts a form straight to `POST /signout` with `client_id` and a `return` address; the server accepts it from that client's own origin (its exact `Origin`, an origin no tenant controls, MT-05 item 1) and returns only to an address the client's metadata document registers (a `post_logout_redirect_uris` entry, as OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 names it, else a redirect URI's origin), ending the session when the cookie came with it and clearing it when it didn't (a different site's form sends no `SameSite=Lax` cookie, so a self-hoster's operator page on another site still clears it); (b) the client sends the person to a `GET /signout?client_id=…&return=…` page with one "Sign out" button, which needs no cross-origin form and costs the person a second click. Recommended: (a), with (b) the fallback the same endpoint serves for any client. Either way a sign-out from any other origin is refused (403) and never ends a session.
- **`prompt=login`** on `/oauth/authorize` (OpenID Connect Core §3.1.2.1): the request shows the sign-in page and goes through the provider even when the browser has a session, and on return replaces the browser's session with the new one; any other `prompt` value the server doesn't implement is refused with `invalid_request` rather than ignored. An operator may use it before what needs a fresh sign-in (billing). Advertise it in the authorization server's metadata (`prompt_values_supported`).
- **A hosted page's sign-out.** The viewer chip of a signed-in viewer offers "Sign out" (trusted chrome, D161): `POST /a/{routeId}/_mostra/session/signout`, behind the shell session, its CSRF token and the shell's own `Origin` (as `session/name` and `session/signin`, D167 item 12), rebinds the route's shell session to the route's anonymous viewer (its derived key, D165 item 8) and refreshes the frame's ticket; drafts and submissions stay with the viewer that made them. It ends only that page's binding in that browser; it doesn't end the API origin's session (the shell has no credential there), so the chip's sign-in afterwards still asks the person to name themselves ("Answer as yourself", once per account and home), now with "Signed in as Ada · Sign out" beside it.
- **The sweep.** Expired `browser_session` rows, `signin` records past their 15 minutes and spent or expired authorization codes are removed by a periodic sweep (the directory keeps only live ones), never inside a request that reads them.
- **The metering window** (#203). `RemoteServerConfig.metering.windowSeconds` (default 60; a value that divides an hour evenly, at most 3,600; anything else `MOSTRA_REMOTE_CONFIG_INVALID`), with every window starting on a multiple of its length since the epoch, so no window straddles an hour and an operator's hourly rollups stay exact. Counters keep their meanings and at-least-once delivery; `bytes.held`'s daily snapshot and first-window rule are unchanged.
- Add MT-06's own decision entry (the sign-out's shape and its origins, `prompt=login`, the hosted page's sign-out, the sweep, the window), the dossier text each item changes (INTERFACES §18.1, §18.4, §18.5, §18.6; DATA_MODEL §7.1; FAILURE_MODEL §11.3, with the shared-computer case), the self-hosting page (signing out, `metering`), the runtime's and the shell's `AGENTS.md` and a changeset. The words a person meets (the sign-out page, "Signed in as Ada · Sign out", the chip's "Sign out") are viewer-facing prose for Mirza's review with the unit's other prose (D149), drafted in `API_PAGE_WORDS` and the shell's words.

## Out of scope

- Signing an account out everywhere (every browser's session, every device link): an operator acts through suspension or `revokeInstanceLink`; a person-facing "sign out everywhere" is a later request.
- Signing out at the identity provider (GitHub's or Google's own session is theirs; a shared computer's person signs out there too, as with any site).
- The CLI, which already signs out (`mostra logout`).

## Acceptance evidence

each change's check through the real interface (a real `mostra-runtime server`, its fake providers, a metadata-document client, the real shell in a real browser), with a seeded violation red on the old code: after a sign-out the next authorization request in that browser shows the sign-in page and calls the provider; a sign-out from another origin than the API origin's own pages and the operator's clients is refused; a GET never ends a session; an operator client's sign-out returns only to an address it registered; `prompt=login` asks the provider though a session exists; a hosted page signed out answers as the route's anonymous viewer and its next "Sign in" asks again; an expired session is gone after a sweep; a ten-minute metering window writes once per window and sums the same; the viewer-facing words are accepted with the unit's prose (D149).

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- A sign-out accepted from another origin is a forced sign-out (logout CSRF): accept only the API origin's own pages and an operator client's own origin, and never by a GET.
- `prompt=login` must never skip consent: a fresh sign-in replaces the session, and consent stays as it was (asked once per account and client).
- The hosted page's sign-out must not leak who signed in before: the anonymous viewer after it is the route's derived key, as for any visitor, with nothing of the account's drafts.

## Handoff

A person can sign out of the server and of every page that signed them in; an operator's own page signs them out of both with one button; an idle server writes as often as its operator chooses. The operating layer's next package wires its account page's "Sign out" to the server's and sets its metering window.
